SERIES 2
SECTION A: 40 MARKS
Answer ALL questions in this section. Each question carries 4 marks.
1. Define Community Service Learning (CSL) and state three key objectives of CSL in schools.
2. List four steps involved in community mapping and explain how community mapping helps identify
service needs.
3. Name five social issues affecting your community and explain how CSL can help address one of
them.
4. Describe the qualities of an effective leader in community service. Give examples of how these
qualities can be demonstrated.
5. Identify three stakeholders in a typical CSL project and explain the role of each stakeholder.
6. What is project sustainability in CSL? Explain two ways in which a CSL project can be made
sustainable after initial implementation.
7. Name and describe two environmental conservation projects that can be undertaken in your school or
community.
8. Explain the importance of monitoring and evaluation in CSL projects. State three methods used to
monitor project progress.
9. Discuss three ethical considerations that should guide community service workers when
implementing CSL projects.
10. What is entrepreneurship in the context of CSL? Give two examples of income-generating activities
that can support CSL projects.
SECTION B: 60 MARKS
Answer any THREE questions from this section. Each question carries 20 marks.
11. Your school has identified that the surrounding community lacks access to clean water for domestic
use. The water point is 3 kilometers away, forcing residents to walk long distances daily. This has
particularly affected school attendance, especially among girls, and resulted in waterborne diseases.
Your CSL class has been tasked to develop and implement a project to address this issue.
(a) Describe how you would conduct a community assessment to understand the water crisis better.
Include the methods you would use and the information you would collect. [7 marks]
(b) Develop a detailed project plan that includes: project goal and objectives, activities, timeline,
required resources, budget considerations, and identified stakeholders. [8 marks]
(c) Explain how you would monitor and evaluate the success of this project. What indicators would you
use to measure impact on the community? [5 marks]
12.A survey conducted in your locality revealed that malnutrition among primary school children has
increased significantly over the past year. Many families lack knowledge about balanced diets due to
poverty and limited access to nutritious foods. Your CSL group has decided to implement a health and
nutrition education project targeting both children and parents in the community.
(a) Design a community awareness campaign on nutrition that includes: key messages, target audience,
communication methods, and educational materials you would use. [7 marks]
(b) Propose three practical nutrition activities that your group could implement to demonstrate healthy
eating. For each activity, explain its educational value. [8 marks]
(c) Identify potential challenges in implementing this project and suggest strategies to overcome them.
How would you ensure the project is sustainable beyond the initial phase? [5 marks]
13.Your school's surrounding environment has experienced severe deforestation and land degradation.
This has led to soil erosion, loss of biodiversity, and reduced water retention. Local farmers have seen
declining crop yields. Your CSL class proposes an integrated environmental conservation project that
includes tree planting, soil conservation, and community environmental awareness.
(a) Outline the specific environmental conservation activities your project would include. For each
activity, explain its environmental benefits and how it would involve the community. [7 marks]
(b) Describe how you would mobilize resources (human, material, and financial) for this project. Include
strategies for community participation and fundraising. [8 marks]
(c) Develop an evaluation framework to assess the environmental and social impact of your project.
What would you measure, and how would you ensure long-term sustainability? [5 marks]
14.Women in your community face economic challenges and limited livelihood opportunities. Your
CSL group plans to establish a women's cooperative that focuses on income-generating activities such as
soap making, vegetable farming, and craft production. This project aims to empower women
economically while generating funds to support other community initiatives.
(a) Propose three income-generating activities suitable for women in your community. For each activity,
explain startup costs, required skills, and potential profit margins. [7 marks]
(b) Develop a business plan that includes: project objectives, target market, production process,
marketing strategy, and financial projections. [8 marks]
(c) Explain how the income generated from these activities would benefit the wider community and
support sustainability. Discuss the role of cooperative leadership in project success. [5 marks]
